stem: A client with suspected lower-extremity peripheral artery disease has a resting ankle-brachial index (ABI) of 0.82. How should the nurse interpret this result?

options.A: The ABI is within the normal range and supports normal lower-extremity arterial perfusion in this clinical setting.
options.B: The ABI primarily reflects impaired venous return rather than the arterial perfusion evaluated by this test.
options.C: The ABI is abnormal and supports reduced lower-extremity arterial perfusion consistent with peripheral artery disease.
options.D: The ABI indicates increased arterial perfusion because ankle systolic pressure is lower than brachial systolic pressure.

rationale: The 2024 AHA/ACC PAD guideline classifies resting ABI as abnormal at ≤0.90, borderline at 0.91–0.99, normal at 1.00–1.40, and noncompressible at >1.40. The current AHA diagnostic page gives the same ranges. Therefore an ABI of 0.82 is abnormal and, in a client being evaluated for PAD, supports reduced lower-extremity arterial perfusion consistent with PAD. C is correct. A misclassifies the value, B assigns the test to venous disease, and D reverses the physiologic meaning of a low ankle-to-arm pressure ratio.
educational_objective: Interpret a resting ABI of 0.82 as abnormal and supportive of lower-extremity peripheral artery disease in the appropriate clinical context.
source_organization: American Heart Association / American College of Cardiology
source_document_title: 2024 AHA/ACC Guideline for the Management of Lower Extremity Peripheral Artery Disease; How Is PAD Diagnosed?
source_version_date: 2024 guideline; AHA diagnostic page updated/current in 2026; live pages retrieved 2026-08-26
source_locator: 2024 PAD guideline: resting ABI should be reported as abnormal ≤0.90, borderline 0.91–0.99, normal 1.00–1.40, noncompressible >1.40. AHA How Is PAD Diagnosed?: same ABI interpretation ranges and ABI compares lower-leg to arm systolic pressure.
source_claim_supported: A resting ABI of 0.82 is abnormal (≤0.90) and supports PAD/reduced lower-extremity arterial perfusion in the appropriate clinical context.
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — diagnostic tests, laboratory/diagnostic values, and potential complications.
correction_summary: Balanced option lengths while preserving the guideline ABI thresholds and arterial-perfusion interpretation.

audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — AHA/ACC explicitly classifies ≤0.90 as abnormal; 0.82 is unambiguously abnormal and no alternate interpretation is defensible.
